Learning targets

  1. I can calculate wire quantities, relevant circuit relationships, power and energy.
  2. I can lay out circuit components and perform demonstrated measurements and inspection.
  3. I can interpret circuit symbols, complete paths, control states and physical wiring layouts.
  4. I can build, diagnose and improve a functioning low-voltage control system.

0–10 min · Brief · Today’s exact job

  1. Why this job: A finished course should show skills each person can perform. Team products provide the context; individual demonstrations establish the learning.
  2. Required today: Run the control exhibition and complete each student’s independent trades-math, measuring and plan-reading check.
  3. Look at the supplied labeled drawing. Find the finished object or test setup before starting.
  4. Read the kit list. Take the listed continuing project out of storage; name missing items before beginning.

Notebook: Title/date; one sentence naming today’s exact object and its purpose.

10–25 min · Measure · Measure and mark

  1. Each student measures one assigned component position or lead route without partner help, naming endpoints and units.
  2. Compare measured value with the student’s final drawing and record signed difference.

Notebook: Feature | required value | actual value | units | datum/endpoints. Keep repeat readings.

25–40 min · Plan · Read the plan and work the math

  1. Mark where your notebook shows an actual repair, retest and calculation.
  2. Read the supplied tolerance transfer problem independently; state both limits before deciding acceptance.

Notebook: Use the named sketch/table in the directions. Label views, dimensions, units and revision.

40–85 min · Make · Numbered bench directions

  1. Set up exhibit with power OFF; teacher inspects connections before operation.
  2. Demonstrate four control states to the visiting crew. Rotate operator, drawing explainer and inspector roles.
  3. Visitor records one specific observation: correct function, unclear step or located mismatch.
  4. Power OFF, correct that exact issue if present and repeat affected states; if none, complete the full final four-state check.
  5. At the teacher station each student: traces one branch; measures a physical dimension; solves the tolerance calculation; explains a named repair and retest.
  6. Record any still-missing skill as pending and complete a focused retry while other students inventory and store equipment.
  7. Power OFF, separate cells only under the kit storage routine, count parts and submit the single individual app response.

Notebook: Label made parts and note any changed dimension. A short labeled sketch is enough; do not write an essay.

85–100 min · Test · Test and inspect

  1. All four control states demonstrated or the remaining fault precisely identified.
  2. Teacher records math, measuring, plan interpretation and build/revision separately for every student.

Notebook: Copy the specified trial table; include each pass/fail or measured value and the change made.

100–110 min · Explain · Show the finished work

  1. Put these on the bench: Completed demonstration, stored kit and individual vocational-skills record.
  2. Final notebook contains drawing, measurement, calculation and real revision evidence.
  3. Complete the independent transfer problem below. These supplied numbers are practice values; they do not change the required build dimensions.
  4. A supplied part is 7 1/4 in ±1/8 in. State the interval and inspect a 7 3/8-in part. Then name one vocational skill you can now demonstrate independently, with evidence.
  5. Save one short individual answer with units, working and notebook page/date. Show the teacher your own physical measurement and plan interpretation. Store the labeled project and return shared supplies.

Notebook: Individual transfer calculation with units + page/date containing the practical evidence.

Teacher inspection points

Use independent / with cue / not observed and record the actual evidence. Offer one focused retry without supplying the answer.

If the build does not work

Time runs out for a student → record the specific remaining check and schedule its completion; do not infer mastery. Product fails → a sound diagnosis is valid evidence but does not become a passing function test.

Worked trades math · supplied practice values

  1. Apply a stated dimensional tolerance.
  2. Target 5 1/2 in ±1/8 in gives 5 3/8 through 5 5/8 in. An actual 5 3/4 in is 1/8 in above the upper limit.
  3. Tolerance is a stated acceptance range; function still needs testing.

Teacher answer key and interpretation

7 1/8 through 7 3/8 in, inclusive; the part meets the dimensional interval. Individual evidence must support the student’s chosen skill.

Individual practical evidence

  1. Math: inspect the individual operation, units and reasonableness check.
  2. Measuring: observe the student place/read the tool using the specified datum and endpoints.
  3. Plan reading: ask the student to find one labeled dimension or connection on both drawing and object.
  4. Build/revision: inspect the actual part, recorded test and named repair. Record independent / with cue / not observed separately; a crew result is not an individual demonstration.

Scope and support

Complete the specified baseline and test first. Only the revision described in this lesson is required. Use a large drawing, fraction strip or oral rehearsal as support, then collect a fresh independent check. Do not fill missing apparatus, dimensions or readings with guesses.
